REGULATION NO 20/R/ICT/RURA/2026 OF 27/01/2026 GOVERNING
TELECOMMUNICATION INFRASTRUCTURE SHARING AND SERVICE
PROVISION IN RWANDA
The Regulatory Board;
Pursuant to Law no 09/2013 of 01/03/2013 establishing the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory
Authority (RURA) and determining its Mission, Powers, Organisation and Functioning,
especially in Articles 2 and 20;
Pursuant to Law no 24/2016 of 18/06/2016 governing Information and Communication
Technologies, especially in Articles 40 and 71;
Upon due consideration and deliberation in its meeting of 27/01/2026;
HEREBY ISSUES THE FOLLOWING REGULATION:
CHAPTER ONE: GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article One: Purpose of this Regulation
The purpose of this Regulation is to establish a regulatory framework governing
telecommunication infrastructure sharing and service provision in Rwanda.
Article 2: Scope of application of this Regulation
(1) This Regulation applies to all licensed companies providing Network Infrastructure and
Network Services.
(2) This Regulation covers:
(a) Siting and sharing of the telecommunication sites;
(b) Sharing of fibre and duct infrastructure in Rwanda.
Article 3: Objectives of this Regulation
(1) The common objectives of this Regulation are the following:
(a) To protect the social and physical environment from potential negative impacts,
while not restricting the development of telecommunication infrastructure;
(b) To minimize disturbance to the environment and loss of service in the provision of
telecommunication infrastructure;
5

(c) To protect the environment by reducing land use as well as infrastructure and
facility installations, while preserving the aesthetic value of the country’s
landscape;
(d) To promote proportionate infrastructure ownership that enhances sharing and
reduces dependency, as well as duplication of investment in network facilities;
(e) To optimize operators’ capital expenditure on supporting infrastructure.
(2) The specific objectives of this Regulation are the following:
(a) To maximize the use of network facilities, including but not limited to network
capacity and capabilities, telecommunication sites, Internet capacity (Layer 2),
ducts, and cores;
(b) To avoid duplication of telecommunication site installations and thereby reduce
visual and noise pollution;
(c) To promote the availability of a wide range of high-quality, efficient, cost-effective,
and competitive telecommunication services throughout the country by ensuring
optimal utilization of telecommunication resources;
(d) To promote efficient sharing of fibre backhaul infrastructure, including dark fibre
and lit capacity, while ensuring service reliability.
Article 4: Interpretation of terms
For the purposes of this Regulation:
(a)“Access Services” means services provided by any telecommunication service provider
or infrastructure provider to another for the purpose of infrastructure sharing;
(b)“Active Infrastructure” means any telecommunication infrastructure which actively
transmits, processes, receives, and manages data, voice, and signal traffic, including
but not limited to base transceiver stations (BTS), antennas, feeder cables, radio access
networks (RAN), microwave radio equipment, switching centers, routers, base station
controllers (BSC), radio network controllers (RNC), backbone transmission networks,
backhauling infrastructure, Internet capacity (Layer 2);
(c)“Authority” means the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA);
(d)“Critical Network Incident” means an incident that causes severe or nationwide
disruption, loss of essential services, or poses a serious threat to public safety, national
security, or critical infrastructure;
(e)“Emergency Services” means fire services and ambulance services;
(f)“Fibre Backhaul” means the portion of a telecommunication network that provides
high-capacity transmission links between access networks, core networks, data centers,
or international gateways, including dark fibre and fibre capacity;
(g)“Fibre Backhaul Sharing” means the provision of access to fibre backhaul
infrastructure, whether dark fibre or transmission capacity, by an Infrastructure
6

Provider to an Infrastructure Seeker under agreed technical, operational, and
commercial terms;
(h)“Infrastructure Lessee” means any licensee who leases network service infrastructure
from an Infrastructure Provider;
(i)“Infrastructure Provider” means any telecommunication operator who provides
shared telecommunication infrastructure and/or co-location space services to another
operator;
(j)“Infrastructure Seeker” means any telecommunication operator who seeks or enters
into an agreement with another telecommunication operator that owns or controls
telecommunication infrastructure or facilities for the purpose of co-location or
infrastructure sharing;
(k)“Infrastructure Sharing” means various kinds of arrangements to share an
Infrastructure Provider’s active and passive infrastructure, including, but not limited
to, the sharing of network elements, systems, equipment, facilities, premises or rights
of way, with an Infrastructure Seeker, subject to an agreement between the parties;
(l)“Law” means Law No. 24/2016 of 18/06/2016 governing Information and
Communication Technologies in Rwanda;
(m)“Lit Capacity” means the amount of actual, usable data capacity currently active on a
fibre-optic cable system, as opposed to the total potential capacity that the cable could
theoretically support;
(n)“Major Incidents” means network events or failures that cause significant degradation
of telecommunication services and affect a large number of users;
(o)“Minor Incidents” means events that cause limited, localized, or short-term service
degradation, with minimal impact on users and no threat to critical services or public
safety;
(p)“Mobile Network Operator” means an operator licensed to provide cellular mobile
services;
(q)“Network Infrastructure Provider” means an operator licensed to provide passive
infrastructure services;
(r)“Network Infrastructure Provision License” means a license granted for providing
network infrastructure as a service;
(s)“Passive Infrastructure” means any other telecommunication infrastructure which
supports signal transmission without actively processing data, including physical sites,
buildings, shelters, towers or masts, electric power supply systems and battery backup,
grounding or earthing systems, air conditioning systems, security arrangements, poles,
ducts, and trenches;
(t)“Power Attenuation” means the reduction in optical signal strength along a fibre link
beyond acceptable thresholds, resulting in service degradation or loss;
(u)“Reference Infrastructure Sharing Offer (RISO)” refers to a standard form Access
Agreement that describes the relevant services offered broken down into components,
and the associated terms and conditions;
7

(v)“Telecommunication Infrastructure” refers to the interconnected facilities, systems
and network elements that support telecommunication services and enable
communication between end-points, including passive and active infrastructure;
(w)“Telecommunication Site” means a telecommunication facility composed of, but not
limited to, towers, poles, power supplies, fencing, air conditioning systems, and radio
access network equipment;
(x)“Telecommunication Tower” means a physical structure designed to support antennas
and other radio equipment used to provide wireless communication services;
(y)“Time to Repair” means the estimated time between fault detection and service
restoration;
(z)“Satellite Cities” are planned urban areas located near a major city (mainly Kigali) and
designed to support it by accommodating population growth, housing, industry, and
services while remaining functionally linked to the core city;
(aa)“Secondary Cities” are major urban centers outside Kigali that are designated by the
Government of Rwanda to support balanced national development and act as regional
economic and administrative hubs.
CHAPTER II: GENERAL TELECOMMUNICATION INFRASTRUCTURE
SHARING PRINCIPLES
Article 5: General Principles for Sharing and Co-location
The following are the general principles governing telecommunication infrastructure sharing
under this Regulation:
(a) Each licensee has an obligation to consider requests for telecommunication
infrastructure sharing, to negotiate such agreements, and to provide infrastructure
sharing services;
(b) When deploying new telecommunication infrastructure, licensees shall give priority to
sharing existing infrastructure before considering the deployment of their own
infrastructure;
(c) In compliance with the Law, licensees shall reach an agreement on infrastructure
sharing through negotiation. Where a dispute arises, the parties may refer the matter to
the Authority for resolution;
(d) Infrastructure Providers shall offer infrastructure sharing services to Infrastructure
Seekers at agreed rates, on terms and conditions that are no less favorable than those
applied by the Infrastructure Provider to itself, its affiliates, subsidiaries, or any non-
affiliated licensee, and of no lesser quality;
(e) Infrastructure sharing rates shall be determined transparently and shall be cost-based,
allowing the Infrastructure Provider to recover a reasonable return on capital,
attributable operating expenditures, depreciation, and a proportionate share of fixed and
common costs;
(f) Infrastructure sharing rates shall not include compensation for loss of business resulting
from the provision of infrastructure sharing services;
8

(g) Costs shall be borne by the Infrastructure Seeker, the Infrastructure Provider, or both,
depending on the nature of the request and as agreed in the infrastructure sharing
agreement;
(h) Infrastructure sharing services shall be provided in a manner that maximizes the use of
telecommunication networks, minimizes environmental impact, and promotes
competition in a timely and economically efficient manner;
(i) Infrastructure sharing services shall be provided at technically feasible points and
routes, on just, reasonable, and non-discriminatory terms, in accordance with an
infrastructure sharing agreement;
(j) Infrastructure sharing under this Regulation shall include both passive and active
infrastructure and shall ensure service continuity.
Article 6: Rights and Obligations of Infrastructure Provider
(1) Any Infrastructure Provider receiving a request for Access Services from an
Infrastructure Seeker shall accommodate such request to the extent technically feasible
and shall negotiate in good faith on reasonable terms and conditions.
(2) The Infrastructure Provider shall consider future demand for infrastructure sharing
when expanding facilities or deploying new infrastructure that is suitable for sharing.
(3) An Infrastructure Provider shall not refuse to provide infrastructure sharing services
except where:
(a) It is not economically reasonable to allow such use;
(b) The sharing is likely to damage the nature or function of the infrastructure, or
(c) Major additional construction is required.
(4) Any refusal shall be subject to assessment and approval by the Authority.
Article 7: Rights and Obligations of Infrastructure Seeker
(1) All Infrastructure Seekers have the right to request access services from any
Infrastructure Provider.
(2) An Infrastructure Seeker shall have the right to request access to both passive and
active infrastructure.
(3) An infrastructure sharing agreement shall not be negotiated or concluded where the
Authority determines that:
(a) Infrastructure sharing would endanger life or safety, irreparably damage property,
or threaten the integrity, security, or interoperability of a telecommunications
network or service;
9

(b) The license issued to the Infrastructure Provider exempts it from the obligation to
provide infrastructure sharing;
(c) The license issued to the Infrastructure Seeker does not authorize it to operate the
network or provide the service for which sharing is requested;
(d) The requested infrastructure sharing is contrary to the laws of Rwanda or the public
interest.
Article 8: Access Service Negotiations
Agreements for Access Services shall be negotiated in good faith between the operators
involved. Where disagreements arise, the parties shall use reasonable endeavours to resolve all
disputes relating to Access Services.
Article 9: General Principle of Access Service Negotiations
The following actions shall be regarded as general principles of negotiation:
(a) Providing all relevant information to the other operator relating to the services sought;
(b) Not demanding charges or fees that are not cost-oriented;
(c) Proposing reasonable terms and conditions;
(d) Not requiring the signing of non-disclosure agreements that are coercive, unnecessarily
broad, or restrictive;
(e) Allowing the inclusion of clauses in agreements that permit future amendments;
(f) Not tying the terms and conditions of an agreement to the resolution of unrelated issues;
(g) Not engaging in actions intended to delay negotiations, including, but not limited to,
repeated refusal to designate a representative with authority to make binding
commitments;
(h) Not engaging in any other conduct deemed by the Authority to constitute a breach of
negotiation principles.
Article 10: Access Service Request
(1) A request for Access Services submitted to an Infrastructure Provider shall:
(a) Be made in writing;
(b) Include sufficient information relating to the requested infrastructure services,
including but not limited to:
i. Infrastructure location (GPS coordinates) or routes;
ii. Proposed date for commencement of negotiations;
iii. Date on which Access Services are required; and
iv. Relevant technical specifications.
10

(2) The Infrastructure Provider shall, within fifteen (15) working days from the date of
receipt of the request, provide a written response to the Infrastructure Seeker.
(3) The Infrastructure Provider and Infrastructure Seeker shall negotiate in good faith and
conclude an Access Agreement within ninety (90) calendar days from the
commencement of negotiations.
(4) A request for Access Services may be refused only on the grounds set out in Article 7
(3) of this Regulation. Any refusal shall be justified in writing and notified to the
Authority.
Article 11: Cost sharing and price setting for infrastructure sharing
(1) Infrastructure Seekers and Infrastructure Providers are encouraged to negotiate and
agree on cost-sharing arrangements for telecommunication infrastructure.
(2) In case of disagreement, either party shall refer the matter to the Authority, which shall
determine the maximum cost-sharing applicable.
(3) The Authority reserves the right to set maximum infrastructure sharing prices, following
consultation with licensed operators, in order to:
(a) Protect competition and consumer interests;
(b) Address sector needs and market trends; and
(c) Enhance competition where an Infrastructure Provider is designated as dominant.
(4) An Infrastructure Provider determined by the Authority to have Significant Market
Power in a relevant market for Access Services shall file a RISO with the Authority for
approval. A RISO shall be filed not later than thirty (30) calendar days after being
directed to do so by the Authority.
(5) The feedback on the review of the proposed RISO shall be provided not later than thirty
(30) calendar days.
CHAPTER III: SHARING OF FIBRE AND DUCT INFRASTRUCTURE
Section One: Allocation of capacity and availability of access
Article 12: Allocation of Capacity
(1) The Infrastructure Provider shall give due consideration to fibre backhaul sharing
requests and shall ensure that capacity allocation does not result in unjustified power
attenuation, service degradation, or discriminatory treatment of Infrastructure Seekers.
(2) The Infrastructure Provider shall proactively plan capacity deployment by allocating
defined portions of total infrastructure capacity for its own use and infrastructure
sharing.
11

(3) To enhance infrastructure sharing, the infrastructure provider shall install at least a 48-
core fibre optical cable for the backbone and 8 cores fibre optical cable for access
network excluding Fibre To The Home (FTTH). This reserve capacity may be reviewed
periodically by the Authority in consultation with all licensed companies.
Article 13: Notification of changes on shared Infrastructure
(1) Any Infrastructure Provider intending to alter, expand, or relocate shared network
infrastructure subject to an Access Agreement shall provide written notice to all
Infrastructure lessee at least five (5) working days in advance.
(2) Such notice shall describe the proposed changes and indicate measures to minimize
service disruption to Access Services.
Article 14: Submission of Rollout Plan
(1) Each Infrastructure Provider shall submit to the Authority, by 31st December of each
year, an annual infrastructure roll-out plan for the following year, indicating major
projects, new and emerging technologies, and geographical areas.
(2) The Authority may require operators to coordinate deployments and explore joint
construction opportunities where infrastructure duplication would be inefficient or
undesirable.
Article 15: Infrastructure mapping and inventory
(1) Infrastructure Providers shall maintain an up-to-date inventory of passive
infrastructure in accordance with templates as updated by the Authority from time to
time in consultation with licensed operators.
(2) Electronic copies of updated infrastructure data shall be submitted to the Authority
within one (1) month following completion of new infrastructure deployment.
Section 2: Obligations of the infrastructure fibre provider and maintenance
Article 16: Obligation with regard to fault repair and restoration
(1) Any fault resulting in power attenuation beyond acceptable thresholds, signal loss, or
service degradation shall be classified as a fibre incident and addressed within the
following Time to Repair:
(a) Minor fibre incidents: up to five (5) working days;
(b) Major or critical fibre incidents causing partial or total service outages:
i. Temporary restoration within four (4) hours in the City of Kigali, secondary
cities, and satellite cities;
ii. Temporary restoration within six (6) hours in rural areas;
12

(2) Where permanent repair cannot be completed immediately, the Infrastructure Provider
shall submit to the Authority, within thirty (30) days, a permanent repair plan detailing
timeline, mitigation measures, and coordination arrangements.
Article 17: Exemption of liability
(1) Service disruptions resulting from fibre cuts or damage caused by natural events, or any
other circumstances beyond the reasonable control of the Infrastructure Provider, and
not arising from its intent, negligence, or failure to exercise due care, shall constitute a
force majeure event.
(2) In the occurrence of a force majeure event, the Infrastructure Provider shall not be held
liable for service interruptions or administrative fines arising directly from such event.
However, the Infrastructure provider shall:
(a) Promptly notify the Authority and all affected Infrastructure Seekers of the incident;
(b) Take all reasonable and necessary measures to mitigate the impact of the disruption;
(c) Restore service in accordance with the fault repair and restoration obligations set
out under Article 16 of this Regulation.
Article 18: Planned works and upgrades
(1) Infrastructure Providers shall plan maintenance and upgrade activities to minimize
service disruption and shall notify the Authority at least seven (7) days prior to planned
works.
(2) Upon approval, affected sharing parties shall be notified prior to execution.
Article 19: Access and non-discrimination
The Infrastructure Provider shall provide access to sharable fibre infrastructure on transparent,
fair, and non-discriminatory terms, subject to technical feasibility and available capacity, and
shall not grant undue preference to itself or any third party in the installation, operation, or
maintenance of such infrastructure.
Article 20: Safety and security
The Infrastructure Provider shall ensure that all infrastructure is installed and maintained in a
manner that protects public workers and property from damage and interference that could
affect the sharing parties.
13

Article 21: Coordination with sharing parties
(1) The Infrastructure Provider shall coordinate in good faith with all authorized sharing
parties regarding access scheduling, fault resolution, upgrades, and operational
coordination.
(2) Such coordination shall include joint fault management procedures, notification of
power attenuation events, escalation mechanisms, and restoration updates for shared
fibre backhaul infrastructure.
Article 22: Continuity and end-of-life management
The Infrastructure Provider shall manage the infrastructure to ensure service continuity
throughout its lifecycle and shall provide reasonable notice and coordination in the event of
decommissioning, replacement, or major reconfiguration.
Article 23: Fibre installation authorization requirements
To minimize visual pollution, any applicant seeking authorization to deploy fibre shall comply
with applicable Ministerial Guidelines on Multi-Utility Channels on installation, maintenance,
and operation of electricity and telecommunication utilities and any other fibre installation
guidelines issued by the Authority.
CHAPTER IV: SITING AND SHARING OF TELECOMMUNICATION BASE
STATION INFRASTRUCTURE
Section One: Site positioning and sharing
Article 24: Compliance principle
All telecommunication sites constructed or located within Rwanda shall comply with the
provisions of this Regulation.
Article 25: Exclusion from the compliance principle
Security organs, emergency services, and any other service deemed necessary by the Authority
are excluded from this compliance principle.
Article 26: Siting alternatives hierarchy
(1) The deployment of a telecommunication site shall be in accordance with the following
siting alternatives hierarchy:
(a) Sharing on the existing telecommunication site;
(b) Development of a new telecommunication site.
(2) Where a new telecommunication site is proposed, the applicant shall demonstrate by
substantial evidence that the existing telecommunication site is not technically usable.
14

Article 27: Telecommunication site design and installation requirements
Telecommunication site design and installation shall comply with the following requirements:
(a) Sites shall be designed and constructed in accordance with internationally recognized
engineering standards and applicable national building codes;
(b) Designs shall account for wind load, seismic activity, and environmental conditions
specific to the proposed location;
(c) Sites shall be designed to blend into the surrounding environment to minimize visual
impact;
(d) Operators shall consider the use of appropriate materials, colors, and designs to reduce
visual obstruction;
(e) In urban areas, infrastructure providers shall consider camouflaged solutions such as
palm trees, monopoles, lamp poles, camouflaged lattice structures, Indoor Building
Solutions (IBS), or other emerging technological solutions;
(f) Guyed mast structures are prohibited. Lattice structures are not permitted in urban areas
unless the applicant demonstrates to the Authority that no alternative structure can
provide an equivalent level of service;
(g) To minimize noise pollution, the primary power source shall be the electricity grid, with
battery backup and solar power as secondary sources. Generators shall be used only as
a last resort and must be fitted with silencers. Exceptions may be permitted subject to a
joint survey and analysis;
(h) The height of telecommunication sites shall not exceed sixty (60) meters in rural areas
and thirty-six (36) meters in the City of Kigali, secondary cities, and satellite cities,
unless a greater height is justified and approved by the Authority;
(i) Any telecommunication site shall be developed in such a manner that it is capable of
accommodating Mobile Network Operator antennas at the top of the tower;
(j) Rooftop installations shall not exceed seven (7) meters above the building and shall be
camouflaged;
(k) Telecommunication sites deployed in urban areas shall use fibre-optic backhaul unless
the applicant demonstrates to the Authority that an alternative solution meets quality of
service/ quality of experience (QoS/QoE) requirements;
(l) All telecommunication sites shall be equipped with aviation obstruction lighting in
accordance with applicable regulations;
(m) To ensure service continuity, every Network Infrastructure Provider shall reserve two
(2) mobile telecommunication sites (Cell on Wheels) for emergency rollout.
15

Article 28: Minimum Telecommunication site access requirements
A Telecommunication site shall have the following minimum access requirements:
(a) All sites shall be accessible;
(b) Safe access routes for maintenance and emergency response shall be provided;
(c) The site access roads shall be constructed in such a manner that the entrance onto any
major rural, town, or private road is consistent with the local authority requirements for
safety and proper drainage;
(d) An exception to access road availability may be granted following a joint survey.
Article 29: Infrastructure protection, security and safety measures
(1) Telecommunications Sites shall be secured with appropriate fencing or access controls
to prevent unauthorized entry.
(2) Any Infrastructure Provider shall have detailed terms and conditions governing access
to facilities or physical infrastructure, including the safety and security standards
implemented by the Infrastructure Provider.
Article 30: Warning and indicative signs
(1) Warning signs indicating restricted access and electromagnetic exposure shall be
clearly displayed.
(2) Every telecommunication site shall provide a readable, indicative sign which shows:
(a) The site owner;
(b) The Site name/Identification (ID);
(c) The Telecommunication site height;
(d) The construction Date;
(e) Emergency phone numbers.
(3) Apart from Warning and Indicative signs, any Signage on a Telecommunication site
shall be subject to the Authority's approval. Any signs placed in violation of this
Regulation shall be removed immediately at the owner or operator’s costs.
Article 31: Power and electrical safety
(1) Power systems shall comply with the National Electrical Safety Standards.
(2) All electrical installations shall include grounding and lightning protection systems.
Article 32: Changes to the telecommunication site
Any replacement, modification, strengthening, or structural change to an existing
telecommunication site shall be subject to prior approval by the Authority.
16

Article 33: Removal of abandoned or unusable facility
(1) Where a telecommunication site is discontinued, or the site owner notifies the Authority
of its intention to cease operations, the Infrastructure Provider shall provide written
notice specifying the intended discontinuation date.
(2) The Infrastructure Provider shall remove the site within ninety (90) days following
receipt of a written removal notice from the Authority.
Article 34: Inspection
Regular inspections shall be conducted on passive and active infrastructure to maintain the
Telecommunication sites in compliance with this Regulation.
Article 35: Public exposure to the electromagnetic radiation (EMR)
(1) Active infrastructure installations shall comply with applicable guidelines on limiting
human exposure to electromagnetic radiation.
(2) EMR exposure levels shall be assessed prior to commissioning and monitored during
operation, where required by the Authority.
Article 36: Fire safety
(1) Fire prevention and protection systems shall be installed where applicable.
(2) Flammable materials and fuel storage shall comply with safety regulations and best
practices.
(3) The Regulatory Authority may conduct technical and safety audits to verify
compliance.
Article 37: Inventory of Telecommunication Sites
(1) For purposes of site sharing, Infrastructure Providers shall submit a complete inventory
of telecommunication facilities to the Authority on a quarterly basis.
(2) National telecommunication operators shall submit quarterly inventories to ensure
regulatory and standards compliance.
17

Section 2: Obligations of the Infrastructure Provider with regard to telecommunication
site operation and maintenance
Article 38: Obligation with regard to the Telecommunication site operation and
maintenance
Active and passive Infrastructure Providers shall:
(a) Ensure continuous service availability, twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days a
week;
(b) Conduct continuous network monitoring and fault management;
(c) Notify the Authority at least seven (7) days in advance of planned maintenance that
may cause service disruption and notify affected sharing parties upon approval. In
emergencies, immediate notification shall be provided;
(d) In case of an emergency, the active and passive Infrastructure Provider shall notify the
authority at least one (1) hour prior to the activity. The maintenance activity shall be
conducted upon approval from the Authority;
(e) In case of major and critical incidents, the active and passive Infrastructure Provider
shall notify the authority immediately;
(f) The notification shall be made to the Authority through telephone call, message, and
email.
Article 39: Maintenance requirements
Active and passive Infrastructure Providers shall ensure that:
(a) Preventive and corrective maintenance programs are implemented;
(b) Response and restoration timelines are defined;
(c) Certified and trained personnel are used;
(d) Maintenance records are maintained;
(e) Access to sites is controlled;
(f) Sites are protected against theft and vandalism; and
(g) Incidents are reported and addressed.
Article 40: Reporting requirement
(1) Active and passive Infrastructure Providers shall submit quarterly and annual reports to
the Authority on site performance and deployment.
(2) Quarterly reports shall be submitted within fifteen (15) days after the end of each
quarter, and annual reports within one (1) month after the end of the year.
18

Article 41: Obligation of the active and passive Infrastructure Providers regarding the
Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE)
Passive Infrastructure Providers shall ensure that:
(a) Electrical and working-at-height safety measures are in place;
(b) Personal protective equipment and safety procedures are mandatory;
(c) Fire detection and suppression systems are installed; and
(d) Environmental protection measures are implemented.
Section 3: Requirements to apply for authorization to install a telecommunication site
Article 42: Application for authorization to install a telecommunication site
Any applicant for authorization to install a telecommunication site shall fulfil the
administrative, technical, and legal requirements.
Article 43: Administrative requirements
Any licensee applying for authorization to install a telecommunication site shall submit the
following:
(a) A duly completed online application;
(b) A justification letter signed by the Infrastructure Provider;
(c) A site motivation letter issued by the Infrastructure Seeker;
(d) A copy of a valid network infrastructure provision license;
(e) Contact details of the applicant; and
(f) Any other information deemed necessary by the Authority.
Article 44: Technical requirements
(1) Prior to application, a pre-survey shall be conducted to find the Telecommunication site
siting location fulfilling the regulation requirements and standards.
(2) The request shall be made by the Infrastructure Provider and submitted to the Authority.
(3) The applicant to be issued an authorization to install telecommunication site shall fulfil
the following technical requirements:
(a) Site Identification and Location:
i. Site name and unique reference number;
ii. Geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) in WGS 84 format;
iii. Administrative location (Province, District, Sector, Cell, Village);
19

iv. Site classification (rooftop or greenfield);
v. Proposed Telecommunication site or structure height.
(b) Technical Documentation:
i. Scaled site layout and design drawings;
ii. Structural drawings of the Telecommunication site, mast, or support structure;
iii. Technical specifications and capacity of passive equipment;
iv. Technical specifications and capacity of active equipment;
v. Power system design and topology (grid, generator, solar, batteries).
(c) Surrounding Environment and Mapping:
i. 360-degree photographic evidence of the site environment at 30-degree intervals;
ii. Google Map or GIS map showing the site and the surrounding environment;
iii. Distance measurements from nearest residential buildings, roads, and utilities;
iv. KML file of the site location and surroundings.
Article 45: Legal requirements
(1) An applicant seeking authorization to install a telecommunication site shall fulfil the
following legal requirements:
(a) Land Ownership and Legal Rights:
vi. Proof of land ownership (land title) or lawful land use;
vii. Sale agreement or lease agreement, where applicable;
viii. Identification documents of the landowner.
(b) Environmental and Planning Compliance:
i. Environmental Impact Assessment Clearance issued by the Rwanda
Development Board;
ii. Construction Permit issued by the City of Kigali or another competent District
authority.
(2) Any other requirements that may be deemed necessary by the Authority.
Article 46: Technical and safety standards for telecommunication sites
Any applicant seeking authorization to install a telecommunication site shall comply with all
applicable technical and safety standards.

CHAPTER V: CONTRACTUAL ARRANGEMENTS AND TIMELINES
Article 47: Reference Contract
(1) All infrastructure sharing agreements between infrastructure providers and
infrastructure seekers shall be agreed upon a Reference Contract, which is in line with
the provisions of the present Regulation.
(2) All Reference Contracts shall include specific provisions on active and passive
infrastructure, backhaul sharing, optical power and attenuation thresholds, Time to
repair commitments, fault escalation procedures, and service credits or corrective
measures for failure to meet agreed service levels, in accordance with this Regulation.
(3) All Reference Contracts shall be made in writing and shall:
(a) Comply with the terms and conditions of the licenses of both parties;
(b) Comply with the Law, or any applicable Board Resolution adopted by the Authority.
(4) A Reference Contract shall not directly or indirectly prohibit or frustrate the provision
of Telecommunication Services that the Infrastructure Provider and Infrastructure
Seeker are lawfully able to provide.
Article 48: Ordering Process
A request for a quotation to provide infrastructure sharing services shall contain the following
minimum information:
(a) The reference number of the Infrastructure Seeker’s license;
(b) A technical description of the requested services;
(c) Locations;
(d) Date required; and
(e) Projected quantities to be ordered with a period of three (3) years forecast.
CHAPTER VI: ENFORCEMENT PROCEEDINGS, GENERAL FAULTS AND
RELATED ADMINISTRATIVE FINES
Article 49: Enforcement Proceedings
(1) Where an incident affecting shared infrastructure occurs, or where the Authority has
reasonable grounds to believe that an infrastructure provider has failed to comply with
the obligations set out in these Regulations, the concerned infrastructure Provider shall
submit an incident report to the Authority.
(2) Upon review of the incident report, or where such report is not submitted as required,
the Authority shall initiate enforcement proceedings and shall notify the infrastructure
21

Provider in writing of the alleged non-compliance, including the factual and legal
basis.
(3) Before adopting any enforcement decision, the Authority shall afford the infrastructure
provider a reasonable opportunity to be heard. The infrastructure provider may submit
representations in writing and/or orally, present evidence and arguments, submit the
incident report or supplementary information, and challenge the evidence relied upon
by the Authority.
(4) After due consideration of the infrastructure provider’s representations and the incident
report, the Authority shall issue a decision in writing.
Article 50: Appeal against any Authority’s decision
(1) Where a licensee is dissatisfied with a sanction imposed, the operator may, within a
period not exceeding thirty (30) calendar days from the date of notification of the
decision, submit a written request for review to the Director General.
(2) Where the licensee remains dissatisfied with the decision issued following the review,
the operator may, within a period not exceeding thirty (30) calendar days from the date
of receipt of the notification of that decision, lodge an appeal with the Regulatory
Board of the Authority.
(3) If still dissatisfied, the licensee may appeal to the competent court.
(4) The Regulatory Board’s decision shall remain in force until a final judicial decision is
issued.
Article 51: Fault and administrative fines
Without prejudice to the sanctions provided for under the ICT Law, general faults and the
corresponding administrative fines are set out in Annex One to this Regulation.
CHAPTER VII: FINAL PROVISIONS
Article 52: Transitional Period
For the existing non-compliant Telecommunication Infrastructure, the licensees have a period
of six (6) months to comply with this Regulation.
Article 53: Repealing provision
All prior provisions contrary to this Regulation are hereby repealed.
22

Article 54: Entry into force
This Regulation comes into force on the date of its signature by the Chairperson of the
Regulatory Board.
